records.name: Mariposa Food Co-op
records.summary: A member-owned natural foods store on Baltimore Avenue in West Philadelphia. Members buy in with a one-time equity payment, get a vote in the co-op's decisions, and can give a few hours a month as working members.
records.what_you_do: Work shifts and committee service, such as governance, policy, or education and outreach committees. Working members get a 10 percent discount.

schedule.text: Working members give at least four hours a month. The site does not list public events or dates.

cost.text: One-time $200 member equity, refundable when you leave (the co-op may hold back refunds to protect its finances). You can pay $25 every three months instead of all at once.

first_step.how: Join in the store, online, or with a printed application, and pay the $200 equity in one payment or in $25 installments. Ask about the open Working-Member Coordinator role or the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee.
first_step.basis: The store is open to the public and the join steps are published, but a vote or a working role needs the equity payment first.

records.notes: Kind set to civic because the vocabulary has no co-op type. The working member page says the program is restarting. The events page lists no events and shows only a 2017 footer year, which is not evidence, so the status rests on a working site with no dates (probably_active, no last_sign_of_life). Store hours not checked.

records.name: South Philly Food Co-op
records.summary: A community-owned grocery on South Juniper Street in South Philadelphia. Neighbors who become members own a share of the store, and anyone can shop there.
records.what_you_do: Help at community events by tabling, planning events, doing marketing or communications, handling handy jobs such as building displays, phone banking, or office support.

schedule.text: Volunteering starts with an online sign-up form. The events calendar did not load for us, so no event dates are listed here.

cost.text: The member equity amount is not confirmed. The join page blocked our reader, and the news articles we read did not state it. The co-op says non-members can shop.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the co-op's site, pick the roles you like, and choose email or text updates. Anyone can shop in the store.
first_step.basis: Open to the public with a clear online sign-up for volunteering, and shoppers do not need to be members.

records.notes: The join page (southphillyfood.coop/join) returned HTTP 403 and was not read, so the equity amount is unknown and not recorded. A search summary gave a $300 figure, but no page we could read confirmed it. The October 2025 news article is the newest dated evidence. Kind set to civic.

records.name: Kensington Community Food Co-op
records.summary: A member-owned grocery on Coral Street in Kensington. The most recent news we found, from February 2023, says members raised money to reopen the store.
records.what_you_do: Shop and take part as a member owner. Current volunteer or work-shift options could not be confirmed.

cost.text: Membership fee or share amount not stated in the news article we read, and the co-op's website did not load.

first_step.how: Check whether the store is open before you go. The co-op's website returned 404 when we checked, so ask around or contact the store directly to confirm how to join.

records.notes: Both kcfc.coop and kcfc.coop/visit-the-store/ returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-08, so the site may have moved or closed. The newest dated item found is a February 2023 news article, which makes the status dormant under the 24 month rule. Kensington is not on the 23 name PACA member directory (philadelphia.coop/membership/). Verify before treating as current. Kind set to civic.

records.name: Greene Street Artists Cooperative
records.summary: An artist-owned live and work building in Germantown with 15 units, a shared garden, and open studios and events. Members are working artists who buy into the co-op when a unit comes up for sale.
records.what_you_do: Visit open studios and events, join the mailing list for news, or apply for membership when a unit is for sale.

schedule.text: Open studios and events happen through the year. The site did not list dates when we read it.

cost.text: Membership means buying a live and work unit and its co-op shares. The listing we read was a $130,000 unit that was under contract.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list on the site for event news. To become a member, watch for a unit for sale and apply through the to-join page, or ask to be put on the waiting list through the contact form.
first_step.basis: Membership needs an artist application and a unit purchase. The public entry points are the mailing list and events, and their dates are not posted.

records.notes: No dated item was found, so probably_active rests on a working site that lists open studios and events. Public attendance at events is implied, not stated. Members include visual artists, theater artists, and writers, so the single interest tag is the closest fit. Street address is not published; Germantown is from the site and an undated student blog list that flags it as a PACA member. Kind set to civic.

records.name: The Energy Co-op
records.summary: A community energy supplier for homes and businesses in Southeastern Pennsylvania that sells wind and solar electricity. Customers who join can vote for the board and help shape its programs.
records.what_you_do: Switch your home or business power to the co-op, vote in member decisions, and attend member meetings, fairs, expos, and talks.

schedule.text: Events on the site include an energy choice overview on October 2, 2026, a fall 2026 member happy hour, and the annual member meeting on June 23, 2026. Several spring and summer fairs and expos are listed without a year.

cost.text: No sign-up, membership, or cancellation fees, according to the co-op's membership page.

first_step.how: Use the sign-up link on the co-op's site or call the office. Joining means switching your power to the co-op.
first_step.basis: Open to any home or business in its service area, with a clear way to sign up and no fees.

records.notes: The membership page does not mention committee service, so no committee role is recorded. The events page does not say whether the public may attend each event. Kind set to civic. An earlier attempt at the http www address returned 403; the https address read normally.

records.name: Philadelphia Area Cooperative Alliance
records.summary: The regional alliance of co-ops in and around Philadelphia, including food, housing, worker, credit union, energy, and artist co-ops. It runs workshops and study circles and keeps the member directory.
records.what_you_do: Browse the member directory to find a co-op, attend a workshop or study circle when one is announced, or give monthly through the Principle Six Club donor program.

schedule.text: Workshops and study circles are announced on the site when they come up. No dated upcoming events were listed when we read it.

cost.text: Workshop costs are not listed. Monthly donations through the Principle Six Club are optional.

first_step.how: Browse the member directory to find a co-op near you, or join the monthly Principle Six Club to support the alliance. Co-ops apply through the membership page.
first_step.basis: No individual membership route is shown. The public entry points are the directory, the workshops, and the donor program.

records.notes: Kind set to network. Its newest dated item is an August 20, 2025 video, which makes the status probably_active. The brief's start URL (pacaphilly.coop) did not resolve, and phillycoop.org did not resolve either; the live site is philadelphia.coop. Its member directory lists 23 organizations, which the file notes break down.

records.name: Home Care Associates

notes: Budget: all 3 WebSearch calls used and 60 of 60 WebFetch calls used (some failed). Result is 11 records (6 publish, 5 hide), short of the 25 to 50 target. The search and fetch budget went to finding the list page (the brief's pacaphilly.coop URL does not resolve), and many co-op sites were blocked, unreachable, or parked, while most of the rest had no public events or join route. PACA's live directory (philadelphia.coop/membership/, newest dated item August 20, 2025) lists 23 organizations with no addresses and no dates. Of those 23: 3 are published (Mariposa, South Philly, The Energy Co-op); 5 are hidden as businesses (ChildSpace, Hivemind, Home Care Associates, Keystone Bicycle, West Philly Scrub); 4 are outside Philadelphia and were not fetched (Bethlehem Food Co-op, Kennett Community Grocer, Newark Natural Foods, West Chester Food Co-op); 4 are blocked or unreachable (Bonfire Media Collective, Catalyst, Praxis Space Philly, Urban Creators); 5 are dropped with reasons below; 1 is Weavers Way (already in the system); and 1 has no website (Accountable History Network, listed as a lead). PACA itself is recorded as a network, though it is not one of the 23. Dropped with reasons (not recorded): A&Associates (worker-owned bookkeeping business, no website listed); Ardent Credit Union (financial institution, not fetched); Sb1 Federal Credit Union and Philadelphia Federal Credit Union (financial institutions, not fetched); Obvious Agency (shop-style site with tickets and no join or volunteer route); Valley Greene Apartments (88-unit housing co-op, no public events or volunteer route shown); Vernon House (resident-owned housing co-op, no events or volunteer route); Friends Housing Cooperative (courtyard events described, but no public attendance or volunteering shown); 2101 Cooperative (housing co-op with visiting hours, no events or volunteer route); Penn Haven Housing Co-op (student housing, newest post 2013); Life Center Association (domain parked). Historic groups named in a 2015 article (Philadelphia Area Cooperative Federation, Philadelphia Association for Cooperative Enterprise) appear defunct and were not recorded. Weavers Way (already in the system, not re-recorded): its committees page (weaversway.coop/committees) names six committees (Environment, Finance, New Economy Incubator on hiatus, Plastic Reduction Task Force, Racial Diversity Equity and Inclusion Advisory, and Emergency Response Network), and none has its own page, so no committee records were made. For the existing Weavers Way record: its working membership page says each household member over 16 owes six hours a year (12 hours cap for a household of two or more), due within the first four months, with a 5 percent discount; committee members earn working member credit after six months of monthly meetings or projects. Board meetings are open to all members. Open items for the owner: whether credit unions and housing co-ops belong in the directory at all (they are member-owned but are not community groups); South Philly's equity amount (join page blocked); Kensington's current status (site 404s, newest evidence 2023); and the PACA start URL in the brief should change to philadelphia.coop.
